source.title: Memorisation versus Generalisation in Pre-trained Language Models
source.authors: Michael Tänzer; Sebastian Ruder; Marek Rei

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how pre-trained language models learn under partial label corruption and refines the picture: BERT first ignores noisy examples, then memorizes them, with a prolonged settling phase. It does not test completely random labels or image inputs.
record.gate_note: The paper varies training-label noise from 0% to 50%, not to 100%. Figure-only curves are not assigned exact values beyond the 30% validation change stated in the text. The reported noise-detection scores are for a proposed detector, not rows about the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests signal-before-noise learning during fine-tuning of pretrained language models, extending V6 to NER. Its noise sweeps also bear on V4, but the supplied text does not establish perfect training fit or steady degradation toward chance. It does not measure V2's time to convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the noise experiments: pretrained models learn general patterns first, retain near-optimal validation performance during a prolonged settling phase, then memorise noise. The full conclusion also stresses poor extreme few-shot minority-class performance and partial improvement from ProtoBERT.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes pre-trained language models on named-entity recognition data with partial label corruption, rather than training image classifiers from scratch on completely random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise level changes the duration of the settling phase; the authors report RoBERTa as more resilient to label noise than BERT and DeBERTa.

fits_no_version.finding: BERT's settling phase lasts longer at lower corruption levels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The duration of the pre-memorisation plateau depends on label corruption; this does not establish time to convergence or V2's optimization-cost claim.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The noise sweep reaches only 50%, not fully randomized labels. Most noise-sweep results are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The task is NER on language data, and the paper does not report a test error at chance.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results omitted. Results on few-shot learning, forgetting rates, ProtoBERT comparisons, and noise-detection F1 are outside the listed versions.

untested.parts: Completely randomized training labels, near-zero training error with chance test performance, and unchanged architecture/hyperparameters for that comparison.
Time to fit true versus random labels, a small constant-factor overhead, and increasing convergence time with corruption. Settling-phase duration is a different timing measure.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Corruption above 50% through complete randomization and chance-level test performance are untested. Perfect final training fit and steady degradation across the tested sweep are not established by the supplied text.
Controlled comparisons of weight decay, dropout and augmentation, including generalization after their removal.
A fully randomized-label condition and a matched true-label versus fully random-label training comparison.

missing.what: Direct noisy-token accuracy during BERT fine-tuning: below random-classifier accuracy during settling, followed by step-like increases during memorisation. Record the phase-specific baseline and qualitative trajectory.
BERT's JNLPBA noise-sweep and first-learning results, explicitly reported as showing the same learning sequence as CoNLL03.
missing.locator: Section 5 footnote 4; Appendix B Figures 13–14; Appendix F Figure 18
missing.versions: V6; V4 for training/validation trajectories, with endpoint uncertainty retained

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source of any listed version. No V4 verdict is warranted from the supplied text: early-stopped robustness does not contradict a claim about training sets fitted perfectly, and unreadable endpoints do not demonstrate incomplete effects. Mixed-version rows require splitting because V6 is observed while V4 remains indeterminate.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error with test error at chance, and the no-hyperparameter-change condition.
The text says settling lasts longer with less noise, but does not report training-time comparisons or a small constant-factor cost.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Noise fractions above 50%, including all labels randomized; whether final training error stays perfect across the full sweep; a numerical, steady test-error rise toward chance.
No comparison removing weight decay, dropout, or augmentation, and no test of whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
Completely random labels and a direct comparison of learning real patterns versus random labels in the original image-classification settings.

rows.subject: BERT-base
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on CoNLL03 training data with randomly permuted labels at varying noise levels, 0% to 50%; measured training and validation F1 over epochs.

conditions.value: AdamW; learning rate 10−4; weight decay 0.01; linear warm-up rate 10%

rows.measure: Training and validation classification F1 during fine-tuning.
rows.baseline: 0% label noise; exact value not stated in text.
rows.value: Figure only for the sweep; at 30% noise, validation performance in the second phase decreases by 0.9%.
rows.note: The text describes a settling phase in which performance remains near optimal, followed by memorization of noise. Noise is varied only up to 50%; the figure gives no exact per-noise values in the supplied text.
rows.check: Split this row by measure/version. For V6, the explicitly described fitting, settling and memorisation sequence is observed. For V4, perfect final training fit and steady validation degradation across corruption levels cannot be determined from the supplied figure text. The 0.9% validation decrease at 30% noise concerns the settling phase, not a fully fitted endpoint, and does not justify a limits_scope verdict.

rows.subject: BERT-base
rows.operation_detail: Measured the distribution of first learning events across training epochs for CoNLL03 examples with varying label noise.
rows.measure: Distribution of first learning events during training.
rows.value: Figure only; the text says BERT learns most learned examples in the first epochs, stops learning new examples in epochs three and four regardless of noise level, and mostly memorizes noise in the last epochs.
rows.note: Learning events are measured for partially corrupted CoNLL03 labels, not fully random labels. The text does not quantify the figure's curves.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report early learning followed by late noise memorisation. Partial corruption and the new task are tested conditions, not evidence that V6 appears incompletely. Most examples being learned early alone is insufficient; retain the authors' identification of late learning as predominantly noise.
